argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate - premises are embedded in comparative exposition rather than formalized

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High - engages with a plausible objection and replies
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High - all moves bear on the central thesis
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate - relies on contested metaphysical assumptions about substance and parsimony

distinctions_drawn: Separate Forms vs categories of opposites
explicit_definitions_given: Primary substance as the concrete individual subject of predication
Potentiality and actuality as modes of the same substance
Contraries as extreme states of a single quality

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: One explicit objection is raised and answered; other objections are implicit
objections_raised: Aristotle's substratum merely pushes the problem back
Plato's account generates a 'third man' regress
Plato's recollection cannot explain physical change

structural_organization.structure_type: Problem → Plato's solution → critique → Aristotle's alternative → objection/reply → comparative conclusion

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that Aristotle's Categories provides a more cogent account of change and predication than Plato's theory of Forms because Aristotle grounds both in immanent primary substance, uses potentiality/actuality to explain transition, and classifies opposites within the categories, thereby avoiding the metaphysical extravagance and inconsistencies of Platonic participation and recollection.
